nodes.label: Craft
nodes.rationale: lightweight ASP.NET Core runtime hosting PowerShell modules as HTTP endpoints, background workers, orchestrators and scheduled tasks; replaces Azure Functions for containerized deployments

nodes.label: Craft.Services Namespace
nodes.rationale: everything in Services/Bridges plus PowerShellRunnerService stays in namespace Craft.Services permanently; downstream PowerShell reaches these types by fully-qualified name; renaming compiles cleanly but fails at runtime with Unable to find type, and TypeForwardedTo cannot rescue it since these types all live in Craft.dll; the containing folder is free to move, the namespace is not

nodes.label: Microsoft.Azure.Functions.PowerShellWorker.HttpResponseContext
nodes.rationale: namespace must match the real Azure Functions worker type because hosted-app routers match on PSObject.TypeNames; all four properties (StatusCode, Body, Headers, ContentType) reach the wire so a handler can redirect

nodes.label: Craft.Hosting.HandlerHeaders
nodes.rationale: normalises header values before they are written: strips CR/LF, drops empty values instead of emitting empty headers, and refuses headers Kestrel computes for itself (Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, Host); headers are cached and replayed alongside status and body so a cached redirect still redirects

nodes.label: PowerShellContractTests
nodes.rationale: asserts every [Craft.Services.*] type PowerShell calls by name still exists, is public, and that nothing unrelated has drifted into that frozen namespace; the only thing turning a downstream-breaking rename into a build failure instead of a runtime one

nodes.label: ConfigurationReferenceTests
nodes.rationale: asserts every default documented in appsettings.example.jsonc still matches the C# default it claims to document, so the example cannot rot into a lie

nodes.label: appsettings.example.jsonc
nodes.rationale: annotated reference listing every config key and its default; documentation only, the .jsonc extension keeps it out of the build glob since it contains comments

nodes.label: Docker build --pull base image floating tag
nodes.rationale: the base image tags float on the 8.0-* minor so .NET runtime security patches are picked up automatically, but only if the tag is re-resolved; without --pull Docker reuses a months-old local base image, and those CVEs live in the shared runtime the base image ships so no package bump fixes them and dotnet list package --vulnerable never reports them; CI sets pull: true
